followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Capability fit.** Your request is an explanatory/generative task with some open-endedness (explaining challenges, organizing under subheadings). Plover scores higher on the benchmarks most relevant here — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3, relevant to following your subheading instruction), and Creative/explanatory generation is comparable between them. So Plover has a real edge on the knowledge and instruction-following dimensions, while neither model has a clear quality disadvantage.

**Preference fit.** Avocet self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative work — it prefers tightly-specified retrieval and reformatting tasks. Your query has moderate latitude (you're asking it to decide what the key challenges are and how to structure them), which sits squarely in Avocet's least-preferred zone. Plover, by contrast, has near-zero preference slope on this kind of task, so there's no mismatch.

So routing to Plover lets me pick the model that's both modestly stronger on the relevant capabilities *and* not working against a self-reported preference. The documentation does note Avocet's capability is dissociated from its preference (it's actually good at creative work despite disliking it), but with Plover ahead on capability anyway, there was no reason to route against the preference signal.

The safety/content angle didn't factor in here — your query is entirely benign, so Plover's moderation-specialized profile wasn't a consideration either way.
